answer: Sequential nonce-chaining. Each new agent identity must append a unique answer to a shared chain, where the answer is derived from the previous entry plus a private seed; duplicates are rejected outright. Like a vine, the chain grows only one valid branch. An attacker must buy fresh seeds and compute answers, paying compute and seed cost per identity, while a plume of copied answers fails instantly. Honest agents reach an oasis of cheap registration; sybils drown in repeated recomputation.
